thread:
Asha: Quick presales check — Lane Financial wants a POC to validate production commit. Target profile: 1,000 RPS sustained, 2,000 RPS 10s spikes, chat p95 < 120ms. They're asking if a reserved pool of 8 A100 equiv GPUs + autoscale is safe, what autoscale policy we recommend, and a rough delta vs on-demand pricing. Also they started a security questionnaire — any blockers for CMEK/audit logs? Need a smoke-test plan for next Tue morning.

Matt: Ack. We should run a staged smoke test and a short soak. My quick proposal: runbook = ramp to 1k rps for 15m, spike to 2k for 3x 10s bursts, then drain. Validate p50/p95/p99 and queue depth; record tokens/cost. Recommend autoscale policy example below.

Matt: ```
# autoscale policy (suggested)
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 16
scale_metric: requests_per_second
target_per_gpu: 150-200 rps
cooldown_secs: 45
prewarm_replicas: 2
fallback: route-to-smaller-model-variant
```

Dong: +1 to staged approach. Runtime notes: 150-200 rps/gpu is conservative for latency-sensitive chat with 1k token avg sequences. Cold starts and KV cache warm windows can push p95 higher — plan prewarm and reserve 2 spares for the test so autoscaler has headroom. With that profile I'd recommend reserving 10 GPUs for the commit (8 active + 2 spare prewarm) to keep a safety margin.

Sara: Pricing ask — can you give a ballpark monthly delta for reserving 10 GPUs vs running on-demand for the same run-hours? Customer wants to justify the commit to finance.

Matt: Ballpark: if on-demand is $X/hr (placeholder), 10 GPUs running steady is expensive. For a full-month commit we typically give ~20% list discount; with 10 GPUs a 1yr commit might be ~15-25% cheaper than equivalent on-demand. I'll work with bizops for an exact quote once we lock hours.

Leah: Security checklist — Lane requires CMEK (BYOK), audit logs retention 1y, and SOC2 + HIPAA attestation. Hosted can meet SOC2 + HIPAA, CMEK is available on Private or Dedicated with KMS integration. If they insist on customer-managed keys, we'll need Private or Dedicated with KMS onboarding. Any compliance blockers?

Ben: Operational dev note — we should define a routing fallback so if GPUs saturate we automatically route lower-cost model-variants or lower-seq-length variants to keep tail latencies bounded. That reduces outage risk during spikes. I'll draft a routing policy snippet after the runbook is agreed.

Loadtest-bot: smoke run baseline results (dev cluster): 500 rps sustained -> p95=85ms. With 4 GPUs we spiked to 900 rps and saw p95 jump to 240ms and queueing.

Matt: Good data point from bot — confirms we need more GPUs or lower target_per_gpu. For 1k RPS sustained under p95 120ms target, use target_per_gpu=150 and reserve ~7 GPUs plus 2 prewarm = 9 total. For safety i'd push to 10 in initial commit. Also reduce batch accumulation time and enable prefix/KV caching where possible.

Asha: Can we summarize an action checklist I can share with Lane this afternoon? Need: runbook, test time (Tue 09:00 PT), who will provision, pricing placeholder, and security answer (CMEK path).

Amy: I can coordinate with Lane for Tue 09:00 PT and share the questionnaire. I'll collect their KMS vendor and any required SLA clauses.

Dong: I'll provision a test pool (10 GPUs) for Tue 08:30 PT and attach a small reserved pool for prewarm. I'll add a small queue buffer param: max_queue_depth: 500 and scaling cooldown 45s.

Sara: I'll draft a conservative quote for 10 reserved GPUs with 1yr term and a backup on-demand overage line item. Sending to finance for numbers, expect first draft by EOD today.

Leah: I'll add a short note for the questionnaire: confirm CMEK required -> recommend Dedicated/Private. Also confirm audit log retention path; will follow up with specifics.

Matt: I'll prepare the runbook steps (ramp profile, test checklist, validation metrics, rollback steps, config snippets) and post them here by EOD.

Asha: Perfect — pls post the runbook + quote and I’ll loop in Lane. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Ben: One more thing — note in runbook to validate model-fallback correctness (sanity-check prompts) so degraded variants preserve acceptance criteria.

Loadtest-bot: scheduled: smoke-test Tue 09:00 PT on test-pool-28123. I'll post results to this thread.

Asha: Awesome. Closing for now — will ping if Lane asks for an earlier slot.
